<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `385deb333d6df6ff23a733d70f0cf41f8691e6e2` — the merge of head `f9dcf30afd057a20a385c8c093262761fc9d3f3b` into base `e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 385deb333d6df6ff23a733d70f0cf41f8691e6e2 && git checkout 385deb333d6df6ff23a733d70f0cf41f8691e6e2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 f9dcf30afd057a20a385c8c093262761fc9d3f3b && git checkout -B drift-repro e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 && git merge --no-ff f9dcf30afd057a20a385c8c093262761fc9d3f3b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6760d275246a4239d5cff46b98a79ff9c0df53e1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts + packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #36794 (body, triage 7118224568, claim 7192981274, amendment 7194794693), the PR-1 record 7195843916 on #37567 with its four nits, this PR's body and 27-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge-base `fbcfdfbb`), and the check-runs on the head. 74 runs: 63 success, 11 skipped, none red, none pending. The two that were still running, `PR-body guards` and `Check Changeset`, were re-read and both ended in success. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` and the PR is a draft. No record and no claim line named this head before this one.

- `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`: one describe sentence on `ImportRowResultSchema.errors`. No accept-set moves. The regenerated references page changes at the three positions that embed the row result, and no `authorable-surface` file is in the diff. Right.
- `BUILTIN_VALIDATION_MESSAGES` gains `import_reference_scope_unqueryable` in en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES. Additive. Right.
- `@objectstack/core` exported `RefMatch` gains one optional member, `scopeUnqueryable`. Additive. Right.
- `@object-ui/plugin-grid` `ImportResult.errors` elements gain an optional `scope`, and the Wizard's default dictionary and all eleven UI locale packs gain `grid.import.referenceOutOfScope` and `grid.import.scopeEntry`. Additive. Right.
- Behaviour: a scoped lookup none of whose candidate reads returned, and that the field-predicate guard did not refuse, now answers `reference_not_found` with the new sentence, runs no unscoped probe and carries no `scope`. Against `main` this moves the formula case from `reference_out_of_scope` back to `reference_not_found`. PR-1's changeset is still pending under `.changeset/`, so no released version answered the other code for it. Right for the declared case. The predicate is wider than the declared case: S1 in ④.
- No removal, no tombstone, no rename, no requirement tightened. Nothing implies an ADR-0087 registry entry.
- The new dogfood file has no CI verdict on this head yet. `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green at PR speed and its shards are skipped there, so the four pins first run in the merge group. Until then they rest on the dev's local reading.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@object-ui/plugin-grid` and `@object-ui/i18n` patch. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right for this diff: the spec half is a describe sentence and a message-catalog key, and neither is something a metadata author writes. `none` takes patch. `Check Changeset` is green on both of its runs.
- The claim amendment 7194794693 reads `added`. That line is about PR-1's `scope` key, which landed in #37567. This PR's file list moves no authorable-surface file.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body. The arm is right: the public surface gains a catalog key a deployment can override and optional type members, and nothing leaves it.
- The changeset body agrees with the tree sentence by sentence, with one exception. It says the new answer is given when "none of its scoped reads could run" and names the formula `param` as the reason. The code tests only the first half. That is S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev flag 1: a formula-scoped column still shows the Wizard's generic "No matching record".** Acceptable in this PR, and a second code is not owed here. The card's acceptance keeps the plain text for `reference_not_found`, and ruling A adds exactly one code. A second `FieldErrorCode` member is outside that ruling. The durable remedy is at the producer: lint refuses a `dependsOn` `param` that names a field the engine cannot filter by, judged with the spec predicate the resolver already uses. That is a narrowing and needs its own card, as the PR body says. This PR closes #36794 and names no such card, so the seat files or names one at ACCEPT (nit N2).

**Dev flag 2: the two i18n census assertions.** Honest updates. Neither gate is loosened.
- `de-quote-pairing-3876`: both pins stay exact equalities and move 133 to 135. The German pack gains exactly two correctly paired spans, one in each new key.
- `untranslated-identity-4376`: `grid.import.scopeEntry` is two placeholders and a pair of quotes with no word to translate, the same class as the `grid.summary.pattern` entry already listed. It is byte-identical to `en` in zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ko, so the file's own dead-entry assertion holds the entry live, and the reason text names those three packs correctly.

**PR-1's nits.** Nit 1 (the `errors` describe and the runner jsdoc) is closed in this diff. Nit 3 (a real engine and the real field guard) is answered by the dogfood file, subject to the CI note in ①. Nit 4 is a prose-face fix for the lane seat. Nit 2 is answered at runtime instead of by lint, with the reason given. The runtime answer is the right shape; its predicate is S1.

**Row access.** The diff changes no access behaviour. Every lookup read, and the unscoped probe from #36735, still runs as the importing caller, and the new path removes a read. The new sentence is composed from the row's own cells and field labels only. Whether the new answer is given depends on whether the reads were refused, never on what any record holds, so it tells the importer nothing about records outside the caller's own read.

**SQL push-down.** No finding. The diff adds no read, materialises no id list and joins nothing in the application.

**`Fixes #36794`** is right: this is PR-2 of 2, and the card's Wizard acceptance is met by `formatDryRunError`'s new case and its four unit pins.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`** holds. The sentence agrees with `ValidateDataIssueSchema.scope` and with emission: `referenceNotFound` sets `scope` on the out-of-scope branch alone, from a non-empty list, and the runner copies it only when set. Its first consumer is the Wizard's `firstCellScope`, which reads element 0, the element the row's `field`, `code` and `error` name.

**`packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts`** holds for the case it names and not for every case the code sends it to. The key is in all four locales with the label, value and scope placeholders, and the jsdoc's composition claim agrees with `referenceNotFound`. The jsdoc and the sentence both state a cause: every read failed because the scope names a target field the engine cannot filter by. The implementing code does not establish that cause.

**S1 (should-fix) — the new sentence states a cause the resolver never checked.**
- `import-runner.ts` sets `scopeUnqueryable` on `scope && !asked && !match.scopeDenied`. That is true whenever every scoped candidate read threw, whatever the reason.
- One reachable case, by reading: an importing caller with no read grant on the lookup's target object. The security middleware answers every `find` on it with a permission denial whose `details` carry no `field_predicate_denied` reason, so `isScopeFieldDenial` is false and `asked` stays false. A read that fails on every candidate for any other reason takes the same path.
- That cell then tells the importer that the lookup's target cannot be filtered by that column and that the field's `dependsOn` needs another one. The column is filterable. The scope can also be the inferred master, where the field declares no `dependsOn` at all.
- On `main` the same cell answers the plain "no record matches" sentence, so this diff changes it. The code stays `reference_not_found` and nothing is disclosed. The defect is a false, misdirecting reason, the class of claim this PR removes for the formula case.
- Fix, either one. Match the refusal positively, as `isScopeFieldDenial` does: both filter doors declare `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'` and `fields` on the refusal, so set the flag only when a refused read names a scope key there, and let every other all-failed lookup keep the plain sentence. Or keep the `!asked` test and remove the cause and the remedy from the sentence in all four locales, the jsdoc, the `RefMatch` comment and the docs line. The first keeps the useful remedy.
- A pin belongs with it: a scoped lookup whose every read is refused for another reason answers the plain sentence.

**`packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts`** agrees with the contract. The `scopeUnqueryable` branch returns before the probe, keeps `reference_not_found`, selects the new key and sets no `scope`. The single-value and multi-value branches both hand in the scoped match. The `RefMatch.scopeUnqueryable` comment infers the cause from the failure; that is S1.

**`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts`** agrees except for S1. `asked` is set only after a read returns, the flag is never set on an unscoped lookup or over a field-guard refusal, and the verdict is not cached, like every other miss.

**`ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx`** agrees. The new case keys on the code and the structured `scope` and never reads the server sentence. With no `scope` it falls through to the server's sentence, the path an unknown code takes. The dry run, the synchronous import mapping, the job mapping and the completion screen all carry `scope`, so the two screens read alike.

Nits, each an accepted deviation or a follow-up. The dev may fold N1 into the S1 commit, since that commit moves the head anyway.

- N1: the sentence's remedy is ambiguous. "That column" reads as the row's column the scope placeholder names by label, and "needs another one" reads as another row column. What has to change is the target field `param` names, as the docs line says. With a two-column scope "that column" names neither.
- N2: no card is named for the lint half of PR-1's nit 2 (dev flag 1 above). Follow-up card at ACCEPT.
- N3: the Wizard joins several scope entries with a hard-coded ASCII comma, inside text that is otherwise localized in eleven packs. The server's qualifier does the same on purpose; the Wizard's own text need not.

No must-fix. S1 is open on this head, so this record does not clear the head for the queue until a delta record closes it.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-zt8cu4`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f9dcf30afd057a20a385c8c093262761fc9d3f3b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts + packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx

Delta review, round 2, from `6760d275246a4239d5cff46b98a79ff9c0df53e1` (record 7204641031: PASS, should-fix S1, nits N1 to N3) to this head.

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #36794 with its three comments, the PR body and 27-file list, record 7204641031, the whole diff from the earlier head to this one (one commit, 21 files), the net diff against `main` (merge-base `fbcfdfbb`), and the check-runs on this head. 74 runs: 63 success, 11 skipped, none red, none pending. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` and the PR is a draft. No record and no claim line named this head before this one.

- `packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts`: the `import_reference_scope_unqueryable` sentence is reworded in en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES, and its jsdoc with it. This PR adds the key, so no released version carried the earlier wording. No key is added or removed by the delta. Right.
- `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`: not touched by the delta. Round 1's judgment stands.
- `RefMatch.scopeUnqueryable` keeps its shape and takes a narrower meaning: it is set only when no candidate read answered and a read was refused with `INVALID_FIELD` naming a scope key. Against `main` the member is still additive. Right.
- `grid.import.scopeSeparator` is a new key in the Wizard's default dictionary and in all eleven UI packs. Additive. Right.
- Behaviour: a scoped lookup whose reads are all refused for any reason other than the two the resolver now reads off the refusal goes back to what `main` does with it. It is a plain miss, and a plain scoped miss is asked once more without the scope. Right; N4 in ④ is about how the prose words that.
- No removal, no tombstone, no rename, no requirement tightened. No `authorable-surface` file is in the net diff.
- The dogfood file still has no CI answer on this head. Its shards are skipped at PR speed and first run in the merge group. The formula pin now passes only if the real doors declare the code and the field list; by reading they do (④), and the dev reports four passed locally on this head.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset still bumps `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@object-ui/plugin-grid` and `@object-ui/i18n` patch, and `Check Changeset` is green on both of its runs. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are still line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset, and still the right values: the delta adds one UI text key and rewords one catalog sentence.
- The rewritten changeset paragraph agrees with the tree: the new sentence is given for an `INVALID_FIELD` refusal naming the scope field, and a lookup refused for lack of read access keeps the plain sentence.
- One loose phrase, on the prose face, for the lane seat: it says every scoped read is refused naming that field. A read whose candidate field the target does not declare is refused naming the candidate instead, because the unknown-name answer comes first. The read by `id` always names the scope field, which is all the resolver needs.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The seat's ruling on S1** (match the refusal positively, keep the remedy text) is implemented as ruled.
- **N1 and N3 ride with the S1 commit**, as the seat had them. Both are judged in ④.
- **N2** is unchanged by this head: the lint card for a `dependsOn` `param` the engine cannot filter by is still owed at ACCEPT. The PR body names none yet.
- **Dev flags from round 1** stand as answered there. The census pins did not move in the delta, and need not: `grid.import.scopeSeparator` holds no run of Latin letters, so the identity census does not read it, and it holds no quote, so the German pairing count is unchanged.
- **Row access.** The delta adds no read. The new test reads the refusal's `code` and `fields` and nothing else. Whether the new sentence is given depends on how the target field is declared, never on what a record holds, and the sentence is still composed from the row's own cells and labels.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The delta materialises no id list and joins nothing in the application.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts`** holds. The sentence now states a cause the selecting code establishes, and its remedy names the right thing.

- **S1: closed.** `isScopeFilterRefusal` reads the refusal's declared `code` and its `fields` (or `details.fields`), never its text. The resolver sets `scopeUnqueryable` only when no read answered, such a refusal was seen, and the field guard did not refuse.
  - The match is live. `findData` runs the ingress filter gate before the engine, and that gate sets `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'` and `fields` on all three of its answers: a name the object does not declare, a dotted path, and a virtual field. The engine's own filter seam sets the same pair on its two. `fields` holds the `where` keys as written, and the scope's keys are `where` keys. The import doors hand the runner the protocol in-process, so the refusal arrives with its properties.
  - At least one read names the scope field. `id` is always a candidate and always declared, so the read by `id` is refused for the scope field itself.
  - Other doors on the same read declare the same pair for a filter field: the internal-field guard, the credential guard, and the stored-metadata body and hash columns. Each refuses every filter over the named field, whoever asks, so "cannot be filtered on" is true there too. A `param` that names no field of the target gets the sentence as well, and it is true of that.
  - What does not match: a comparand the field's type cannot take answers `INVALID_FILTER`, a driver fault answers its own code, and a missing grant answers a permission denial. None of them is taken for the scope.
  - A mixed answer cannot mislead. The filter doors judge the declaration alone and run before the permission middleware, so with an unfilterable scope every read is refused there, and with a filterable one none is. If the mix did occur, the flag still needs a refusal that names a scope key, which is a fact about the field for every caller. A field-guard refusal ends the loop and wins. One answered read keeps the normal path.
  - Both pins asked for are in: every read refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` naming no field, and every read refused `INVALID_FIELD` naming a field outside the scope. Each answers the plain sentence. The fake refusals carry the same properties the real doors set.
- **N1: closed.** All four locales now name the target field the `dependsOn` entry filters by and tell the author to point that entry at a stored field. The jsdoc says the remedy never names a row column. Residue, accepted: with two `dependsOn` entries the sentence does not say which one, and "stored" is loose for a field that is stored but withheld. The action it asks for is right in both cases.
- **N4**, new, a nit. The jsdoc here says any other refusal "keeps the plain sentence", and the changeset and the docs line say the same. The tree keeps a plain miss, as the `RefMatch` comment says exactly, and `referenceNotFound` then asks without the scope as it does for any scoped miss. A refusal that has nothing to do with the scope refuses that second read too, so the plain sentence follows, as pinned. A refusal caused by the scope cell's value (`INVALID_FILTER`) leaves the second read free to answer, and that cell answers `reference_out_of_scope`. This is what `main` does today, and the claim is not false there: a value the field's type cannot take matches no record. It has no effect on correctness. Accepted deviation; the N2 card can carry one line on it, to skip the second read whenever no scoped read answered.

**`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`** is unchanged since round 1 and holds as judged there.

**`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts`** agrees with the contract. The flag is read off declared properties, set only on a scoped lookup, never over a field-guard refusal, and never cached.

**`packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts`** agrees. Only comments moved, and they now say what the runner does.

**`ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx`** agrees.

- **N3: closed.** The entries are joined by `t('grid.import.scopeSeparator')`. The values are right for each pack and match the separators those packs already carry (`partSeparator`, `nameSeparator`): `、` in ja, zh-Hans and zh-Hant, `، ` in ar, `, ` in the other seven. The Wizard falls back per key, so a host dictionary without the key gets the default. The pin uses a separator that is not a comma.

N2 stays a follow-up card at ACCEPT. N4 is an accepted deviation.

No must-fix. No should-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-zt8cu4`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head f9dcf30afd · card #36794 · area s2-data · 2026-11-26T23:22Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and relation.** `l1-face.mjs --pr 37706` read 13 items and flagged none; 74 check-runs on this head, 63 success, 11 skipped, none red or pending. The dogfood shards skip at PR speed, so the real-engine formula pin first runs in the merge group; the dev reports it green locally and the reviewer confirmed by reading that the doors it relies on declare the matched code and fields.
- **`Fixes #36794` is right (PR-2; PR-1 #37567 merged).** An import value outside the row's lookup scope now reads `reference_out_of_scope` in the wizard in 11 locales; a scope the target cannot be filtered on answers its own sentence only when a filter door refuses naming the scope field (positive match on the declared `INVALID_FIELD` and `fields`), and every other refusal keeps the plain "no matching record". PR-1's nits 1, 3 and 4 are closed; nit 2 is answered at run time here, its lint half goes to the follow-up card.
- **Contract review.** Record 7204641031 PASS with S1 open → delta 7205472092 on this head: PASS, S1, N1, N3 closed, no must-fix, no should-fix. N2 (lint on `dependsOn.param`) and N4 (skip the unscoped probe when no scoped read answered) go to follow-up card #37717. Adopted. No row-access change: every read still runs as the importing caller.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (a catalog key and optional type members); `Metadata-protocol: none` (`export.zod.ts` changes one describe sentence; no authorable-surface file); `patch` on four packages. True.
- **Governance.** `check-governed-merges.mjs`: not governed. Tier S.

Tier: S. Landing: ready + auto-merge by this stroke.
